distinguishing_features: Engineered micro-pinhole/reentrant cavities on the vessel wall to pin heterogeneous ice nucleation at a specific predicted temperature
Deterministic, spatially localized phase transition replacing stochastic supercooling burst in cryopreservation
Tuning site radius and contact angle to set nucleation onset temperature
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to make the onset of the phase transition reproducible and spatially controlled so that latent heat release does not cause damaging thermal shock and mechanical shear.
parsed.viable_reason: Controlled heterogeneous nucleation via engineered surface features is physically sound, testable with standard freezers and thermocouples, and uses feasible laser-etched vial geometry.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 2 uses halogen chemistry to suppress heterogeneous wall nucleation, so deliberately designing nucleation sites to trigger deterministic onset is a non-routine departure, not a parameter tweak of that approach.
